summary: Multiple explosions struck Iranian military sites including the Konarak naval base attacked by enemy fighter jets, while Israel eliminated two Hamas operatives involved in the October 7 attacks. The U.S. revealed Israel shared intelligence on an Iranian plot to assassinate Donald Trump, prompting strike preparations before opting for diplomacy. Turkey finalized S-400 sales to the UAE to unlock F-35 access, altering regional defense dynamics.
key_points: Iran's Konarak naval base in Sistan and Baluchestan was attacked in two phases by enemy fighter jets on July 9, 2025, per the county governor. (Source: @shin_persian/7624)

Explosions reported in Ahvaz, Bushehr, Bandar Abbas, and Konarak, with Iranian media citing a military site on Bushehr's outskirts hit by a projectile. (Source: @inon_yttach/9355, @VahidOnline/76902, @shin_persian/7617, @inon_yttach/9354)
IDF and Shin Bet killed Yahya Saeed Muhammad Hamdan, head of a Nukhba cell that infiltrated Reim base on October 7. (Source: @almogboker78/17693)
IDF and Shin Bet eliminated Wahid Abu Salam, former Khan Yunis western company commander who participated in kidnappings on October 7. (Source: @almogboker78/17687)
Hamas spokesman Hazem Qassem survived an assassination attempt in Gaza City; his bodyguard was killed and he was critically wounded. (Source: @yediotnews25/132492)
CNN reported Israel gave the U.S. intelligence on a specific Iranian plot to assassinate Donald Trump; U.S. prepared strikes Thursday but chose diplomacy. (Source: @VahidOnline/76911)
Turkey finalized sale of its Russian S-400 systems to the UAE, aiming to lift CAATSA sanctions and rejoin the F-35 program. (Source: @amitsegal/62940, @Faytuks_Network/4805)
Ali Khamenei was buried in Mashhad's Imam Reza shrine after 131 days; funeral prayer led by his son Mustafa, with successor Mojtaba absent. (Source: @VahidOnline/76903, @VahidOnline/76910)

points: The governor of Konarak County confirmed a military installation at the Konarak naval force was attacked in two phases by enemy fighter jets on July 9, 2025 at 21:10 local time (1740Z) in Sistan and Baluchestan province. (Source: @shin_persian/7624)

Local reports and Iranian media cited explosions in Ahvaz (southwest), Bushehr (south), Bandar Abbas (Hormozgan), and Konarak, with a military site on Bushehr's outskirts reportedly hit by a projectile attributed to 'American-Zionist enemy.' (Source: @inon_yttach/9355, @VahidOnline/76902, @shin_persian/7617, @inon_yttach/9354)
Basij forces were targeted and killed at two IRGC checkpoints in Mashhad, according to social media images. (Source: @shin_persian/7623)

A member of Iran's Supreme National Security Council warned that if infrastructure is targeted, Iran will respond in kind, and the 'criminal Zionist entity will not be immune from fighters' response.' (Source: @rasedal3ado138e/375940)
Parliament national security committee member Kothari stated the UAE 'will pay the price for its cooperation with the United States.' (Source: @rasedal3ado138e/375913)
Former intelligence minister Younesi claimed Mossad has infiltrated various parts of the country and warned officials to fear for their lives. (Source: @kianmeli1/88661)

IDF and Shin Bet announced the elimination of Yahya Saeed Muhammad Hamdan, head of a Nukhba cell in Hamas's military wing that infiltrated the Reim base during the October 7 massacre, who had recently promoted terror plans against IDF forces. (Source: @almogboker78/17693)

IDF and Shin Bet killed Wahid Abu Salam, former commander of the western company in Khan Yunis, who participated in the October 7 infiltration, kidnapping of Israeli civilians, and holding them hostage in southern Gaza. (Source: @almogboker78/17687)

Prime Minister Netanyahu spoke with President Trump, continuing coordination; Trump updated on U.S. moves in the Gulf, while Netanyahu raised the severity of Erdogan's statements against Israel's existence and the need for security zones on Israel's borders. (Source: @New_security8200/202395)
Israel shared intelligence with the U.S. this week showing Iran recently prepared a specific plot to assassinate Donald Trump, per CNN citing two knowledgeable sources. (Source: @VahidOnline/76911)

sections.threat_assessment: Iran faces simultaneous pressure from apparent Israeli or U.S. strikes on multiple military sites, including a naval base attacked by fighter jets, while its leadership transition after Khamenei's burial creates potential instability. The explicit Iranian threat of reciprocal infrastructure targeting and warnings to the UAE indicate a widening confrontation. Israel's demonstrated capability to eliminate Hamas leaders in Gaza and share actionable intelligence on Iranian assassination plots suggests an intensified campaign. The U.S. maintaining target lists in Iran while pausing strikes for diplomacy creates a volatile deterrence posture that could shift rapidly.
sections.regional_response: Turkey's S-400 sale to the UAE represents a significant realignment, potentially easing Turkey's Western relations while bolstering Gulf air defenses. Qatar's active mediation in Tehran and with Washington shows Gulf states seeking de-escalation. The Kremlin's sensitivity to the S-400 sale reflects Russian concerns over technology transfer. Iran's internal warnings about Mossad infiltration and threats against the UAE signal a regime preparing for asymmetric retaliation. Hamas leadership's relocation to Turkey indicates a strategic shift in the group's external operations.
sections.intelligence_notes: The Konarak naval base attack by fighter jets suggests a significant escalation in kinetic action against Iranian military infrastructure, possibly testing air defenses. The precision in eliminating specific Hamas operatives tied to October 7 indicates high-quality Israeli human intelligence in Gaza. The U.S. disclosure of the Trump assassination plot intelligence serves both as a deterrence signal and a diplomatic lever. The 131-day delay in Khamenei's burial and Mojtaba's absence raise questions about succession stability. The convergence of Qatari, Turkish, and U.S. diplomatic tracks suggests a coordinated but fragile effort to manage escalation.
